properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued July 31 at 11:30PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 1128 PM CDT/1028 PM MDT/, Doppler radar was tracking a strong
outflow boundary located along a line extending from 16 miles west
of Eunice Airport to near Loving to 10 miles east of Lincoln
National Forest. Movement was south at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs, and blowing dust
may briefly reduce visibility down to 2 miles or less.

Locations impacted include...
Carlsbad, Pine Springs, Loving, McKittrick Canyon, Avalon, Maljamar,
Seven Rivers Airport, Brantley Lake State Park, Red Bluff Reservoir,
Orla, Carlsbad Caverns National Park, Malaga, Carlsbad North,
Guadalupe Mountains National Park, Whites City, Lincoln National
Forest, Loco Hills, Otis, Dayton, and Halfway.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 1 at 12:24AM EDT until August 1 at 4:30AM EDT by NWS Gaylord MI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of northern Michigan, including the following
counties, Cheboygan and Presque Isle.

* WHEN...Until 430 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1224 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the
advisory area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Onaway, Indian River, Aloha, Aloha State Park, Koehler
Township, Mullet Lake, Topinabee, Tower, Onaway State Park
and Riggsville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 31 at 10:35PM CDT until August 1 at 12:00AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southern Crawford County in east central Missouri...
Southern Washington County in east central Missouri...

* WHEN...Until midnight CDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1034 PM CDT, the thunderstorms producing the heavy rainfall
had ended, but areas of minor flooding will continue as the water
drains into creeks and rivers.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Potosi, Steelville, Irondale, Mineral Point, Courtois,
Cherryville, Caledonia, Davisville, Shirley, Dillard, Latty,
Belgrade, Cook Station and Cadet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 10:34PM CDT until July 31 at 11:45PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
At 1034 PM CDT, the thunderstorms producing heavy rain had ended.
However, flash flooding is likely to continue as the water drains
into creeks and rivers.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sullivan, Cuba, Bourbon, Anthonies Mill, Leasburg, Richwoods, Old
Mines, St. Cloud and Oak Hill.

This includes the following State Parks...
Washington State Park and Onondaga Cave State Park.

This includes Interstate 44 in Missouri between exits 203 and 218.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:52PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden, Three Rivers...Major
flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.2 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 39.0
feet on 10/21/2013.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 31 at 9:32AM PDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Monday August 3.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
